titulo: A higher floor, a quieter room, and a later checkout
subtitulo: You paid online, the desk wants your passport and your home address, and the four things you ask for before you unpack decide the rest of the week
cena: Half past two, the desk has your booking on the screen, the room is not ready until four, and everything you will get out of this hotel is decided in the next forty seconds.

clique.desconto: Nobody handed you those four sentences. You built them out of words you already had.
clique.piso: You will ask a Spanish hotel for four things before you unpack. Most people who spend a fortnight here ask for none of them and put it in the review instead.

frasePiso: You will ask a Spanish hotel for four things before you unpack. Most people who spend a fortnight here ask for none of them and put it in the review instead.
permissao: You are allowed to ask on the way in, before anything has happened: a quieter room, a higher floor, your bags held until four, one more towel, a later checkout. A room swap for noise is the most ordinary request that desk hears all year, and asking early is not a complaint — it is what the desk would rather you did.
espelho: Saying nothing for four nights and then writing it up online afterwards is the bit that reads as odd there. The complaint that arrives after you have gone is the only one nobody could have fixed.

fichasCulturais.sinal: The receptionist asks for your mobile number, your e-mail and the address of the house you live in, and types all of it into a form.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: No hotel at home has ever wanted my home address. Either this place is careless with my data or somebody is building a list.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Since December 2024 every place that puts you up — and every car hire desk — has to record that data and report it to the security forces. The person at the desk has no discretion about it: no data, no room.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Have the passport out before he asks, let him scan it, read your own number off your screen, and stop apologising for the address.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You are upstairs in three minutes instead of ten, and you stop suspecting the one desk in the country whose job is to be on your side.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Nowhere else. A bar, a shop or a museum has no business asking where you live, and the only other counter in Spain with the same duty is the car hire desk.

fichasCulturais.sinal: One in the morning, the terrace under your window is fuller than it was at nine, and there are children in the square.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Something has gone wrong down there. And if I ring down about it I become the difficult foreigner in room three-oh-two.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The street outside empties much later than you would ever guess, so that desk expects to move somebody most nights of the year. A room swap costs them one lift ride and a new key.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Walk down on the first night, say what you can hear, and ask for the swap in that order — what is happening first, what you want second.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get the inside room on night one instead of night four, and you sleep for the rest of the week.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not in a six-room guesthouse with nothing free — there the honest answer is that there is nowhere to move you, and the thing worth asking for is a fan and earplugs.

aprofundar.titulo: The desk, the tax and the room (optional reading)

secoes.titulo: Ask on the way in, not on the way out
secoes.corpo: Every request in this part is cheaper at check-in than at any point afterwards, and for the same reason: at half past two the desk still has the whole board in front of it. A quieter room, a higher floor, a late checkout and a held bag are all decisions somebody makes by looking at a screen, and by six in the evening the screen has filled up. This is also why the order of the sentence matters when something is wrong: say what is happening first ('hay mucho ruido') and what you want second ('¿tienen otra habitación?'). The desk is not deciding whether to believe you; it is deciding what it has free. 'Quería otra habitación, si es posible' and 'quería una habitación más tranquila, si es posible' are the same move: the opening word and the closing three never move, and only the thing in the middle changes — and 'si es posible' is not padding here, it is the phrase that turns a demand into a question somebody can say yes to.

exemplos.es: ¿A qué hora es la entrada / la salida?
exemplos.pt: lah en-TRAH-dhah · lah sah-LEE-dhah — check-in / check-out time. 'Check-in' and 'check-out' are understood everywhere too.
PWEH-dhoh ah-THEHR el chek-AWT mahs TAR-deh — can I check out later? Asked on day one it is usually free; asked on the day it is a favour.

secoes.titulo: Why they want your e-mail and your home address
secoes.corpo: Spain's Royal Decree 933/2021 (BOE-A-2021-17461), compulsory since 2 December 2024, requires accommodation providers — and car hire companies — to record and report to the security forces: full name, passport or ID document, nationality, sex, date of birth, phone, e-mail, full home address, number of travellers and, where minors are involved, the relationship between them. That is why the form is long, why it is sometimes only in Spanish, and why the receptionist does not look apologetic about it. It is not negotiable and it is not aimed at you: no data, no room. Hand over the passport, let them scan it, and move on. The one place you will meet the same duty again is the hire car counter.

exemplos.pt: neh-theh-SEE-tah mee pah-sah-POR-teh — do you need my passport?
ah-KEE TYEH-neh — here you are. Do you need anything else?

secoes.titulo: The tourist tax, and where it actually bites
secoes.corpo: It is regional, not national. Catalonia and the Balearics have charged it for years, and the Basque Country joined in 2026. In Barcelona the total for a five-star hotel reached €12 a night from 1 April 2026, with the municipal surcharge on a published schedule to keep climbing towards 2029 — our source gives that figure as a nightly total and does not say per person, so treat the per-person question as one to ask at the desk. In the Balearics the announced increase never came into force, so it remains roughly €1 to €4 per person per night by hotel category, plus VAT on the tax itself. You will also see the Canary Islands listed on some aggregator sites — that one is genuinely contested and our own research flags it as unconfirmed, so do not assume either way: ask at the desk. The tax is almost never inside the price you paid on a booking site, and it is often collected in cash on the way out.

exemplos.pt: lah TAH-sah too-REES-tee-kah — is the tourist tax included?
seh PAH-gah ah-PAR-teh — is it paid separately? In cash?

secoes.titulo: Everything else you can hang on 'no funciona'
secoes.corpo: The shape is [thing] + 'no funciona', and the thing always arrives wearing its article. Learn the article and the word together and you never have to think about gender again — say 'la problema' and you will still get exactly what you asked for; gender is the most forgiving mistake in Spanish. You will also meet the same phrase written on machines all over the country: 'NO FUNCIONA', 'FUERA DE SERVICIO' and 'AVERIADO' all mean out of order, on lifts, ticket machines and petrol pumps. And when the thing is not a machine, the sentence changes at the front instead of the end: 'no hay' — there isn't any. No hay agua caliente, no hay toallas, no hay papel. One more pair worth having: 'la entrada' and 'la salida' are check-in and check-out on a hotel form, and the way in and the way out on a door. At the airport only the second one carries over — 'SALIDAS' is departures, while arrivals is 'LLEGADAS', not 'entradas'.

exemplos.es: La llave no funciona. / El ascensor no funciona.
exemplos.pt: lah YAH-beh · el ah-then-SOR — the key / the lift isn't working

exemplos.es: No hay toallas. / No hay papel.
exemplos.pt: noh ai toh-AH-yahs · noh ai pah-PEL — there are no towels / there's no paper
